struct task_struct objects are a bit interesting in terms of how their
lifetime is protected by refcounts. task structs have two refcount
fields:
1. refcount_t usage: Protects the memory backing the task struct. When
this refcount drops to 0
waiting for an RCU grace period to elapse. This is the field that
most callers in the kernel currently use to ensure that a task
remains valid while it's being referenced
tracked with bpf_task_acquire() and bpf_task_release().
2. refcount_t rcu_users: A refcount field which
schedules an RCU callback that drops a reference held on the 'usage'
field above (which is acquired when the task is first created). This
field therefore provides a form of RCU protection on the task by
ensuring that at least one 'usage' refcount will be held until an RCU
grace period has elapsed. The qualifier ""a form of"" is important
here
column2: as a task can remain valid after task->rcu_users has dropped to

column1: 0 and the subsequent RCU gp has elapsed.
In terms of BPF
column2: we want to use task->rcu_users to protect tasks that

column1: function as referenced kptrs
column2: and to allow tasks stored as referenced

column1: kptrs in maps to be accessed with RCU protection.
Let's first determine whether we can safely use task->rcu_users to
protect tasks stored in maps. All of the bpf_task* kfuncs can only be
called from tracepoint
types. For tracepoint and struct_ops programs
passed to a program handler will always be trusted
safe to call bpf_task_acquire() with any task passed to a program.
Note
column3: that we must update bpf_task_acquire() to be KF_RET_NULL

column1: as it is possible that the task has exited by the time the program is
invoked
column2: even if the pointer is still currently valid because the main

column1: kernel holds a task->usage refcount. For BPF_PROG_TYPE_SCHED_CLS
should never be passed as an argument to the any program handlers
should not be relevant.
The second question is whether it's safe to use RCU to access a task
that was acquired with bpf_task_acquire()
column2: and stored in a map. Because

column1: bpf_task_acquire() now uses task->rcu_users
column2: it follows that if the task

column1: is present in the map
column2: that it must have had at least one

column1: task->rcu_users refcount by the time the current RCU cs was started.
Therefore
column2: it's safe to access that task until the end of the current

column1: RCU cs.
With all that said
column2: this patch makes struct task_struct is an

column1: RCU-protected object. In doing so
be KF_ACQUIRE | KF_RCU | KF_RET_NULL
necessary. A subsequent patch will remove bpf_task_kptr_get()
bpf_task_acquire_not_zero() respectively.
